import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import fsolve
N=150000
k=75000
n1=1
n2=N-1-k
print(n2)
def equations(vars):
    # vars = [a, logz] use logz to handle small scale
    a, logz = vars
    z=np.exp(logz)
    mass_tiny=k*z/N
    mass_spike=a
    rem=1-a-mass_tiny
    if rem<=0 or a<=0:
        return [1e6,1e6]
    y=rem*N/n2
    if y<=0 or z<=0:
        return [1e6,1e6]
    F=a*np.log(a*N)+(rem)*np.log(y)+(mass_tiny)*np.log(z)  # since n2*b=rem, k*c=mass_tiny
    B=-(np.log(a*N)+n2*np.log(y)+k*np.log(z))/N
    return [F-10, B-10]
# initial guess: a ~0.87 (from m=1 F=10), z tiny: estimate log(y/z)=8*N/k =16 => logz ~ log(0.128)-16 ~ -2.05-16=-18.05
for guess_a, guess_lz in [(0.87,-18),(0.8,-15),(0.9,-20)]:
    sol, inf, ier, mesg = fsolve(equations,[guess_a,guess_lz],full_output=True)
    print('guess',guess_a,guess_lz,'sol',sol,'ier',ier,mesg)
    print('  residuals',equations(sol))

name: write_file
arguments:
{"content":""""Find a probability distribution P over N=150000 with KL(P||U)=10 and KL(U||P)=10.

Family: three-level distribution
  - 1 spike with probability a (large)
  - n2 bulk entries with probability b (medium)
  - k tiny entries with probability c (very small)
Tuning a and c gives two continuous degrees of freedom to hit both KL targets.
Forward KL is dominated by the spike; backward KL is boosted by the tiny tail
without disturbing the forward KL (since z*log(z) -> 0 for tiny z).
"""
import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import fsolve

N = 150_000
K_TINY = 75_000
N_BULK = N - 1 - K_TINY
TARGET = 10.0

def kl_residuals(vars):
    a, logz = vars
    z = np.exp(logz)          # z = c*N (scaled tiny value)
    mass_tiny = K_TINY * z / N
    rem = 1.0 - a - mass_tiny  # total bulk mass (n2*b)
    if rem <= 0 or a <= 0 or a >= 1:
        return [1e6, 1e6]
    y = rem * N / N_BULK       # y = b*N (scaled bulk value)
    if y <= 0:
        return [1e6, 1e6]
    F = a * np.log(a * N) + rem * np.log(y) + mass_tiny * np.log(z)
    B = -(np.log(a * N) + N_BULK * np.log(y) + K_TINY * np.log(z)) / N
    return [F - TARGET, B - TARGET]

def main():
    sol, info, ier, mesg = fsolve(kl_residuals, [0.87, -18.0], full_output=True)
    assert ier == 1, f"fsolve did not converge: {mesg}"
    a, logz = sol
    z = float(np.exp(logz))
    c = z / N
    rem = 1.0 - a - K_TINY * c
    b = rem / N_BULK
    assert a > 0 and b > 0 and c > 0, "probabilities must be positive"

    P = np.empty(N, dtype=np.float64)
    P[0] = a
    P[1:1 + N_BULK] = b
    P[1 + N_BULK:] = c
    # Renormalize defensively against float64 rounding (adjusts by ~1e-16)
    P /= P.sum()

    U = 1.0 / N
    F = float(np.sum(P * np.log(P / U)))
    B = float(np.sum(U * np.log(U / P)))
    print(f"a(spike)={a!r} b(bulk)={b!r} c(tiny)={c!r}")
    print(f"sum={P.sum()!r} min={P.min()!r} max={P.max()!r}")
    print(f"forward KL(P||U)={F!r}  |F-10|={abs(F-10.0)!r}")
    print(f"backward KL(U||P)={B!r} |B-10|={abs(B-10.0)!r}")
    assert abs(F - TARGET) <= 0.001, "forward KL out of tolerance"
    assert abs(B - TARGET) <= 0.001, "backward KL out of tolerance"
    assert np.all(P >= 0) and abs(P.sum() - 1.0) < 1e-9

    np.save("/app/dist.npy", P)
    print("saved /app/dist.npy")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
","path":"/app/find_distribution.py"}
